title: A lifelong learner
tomorrow: a grown man sits with the kids to learn. what does he read first?

lines: NO REST, IN THIS WORLD OR THE NEXT.
cards: The last college application goes in, the screen says submitted, and the cap-and-gown photo is only months away. Done with school forever, Noa announces at dinner, more or less. Her grandfather, Saba David, laughs.
Not unkindly. In this tradition, he tells her, nobody graduates. The Talmud says those who study have no rest, not in this world and not in the next.
That sounds exhausting, until you hear the verse it leans on.

teach.b: "They go from strength to strength." That's the Psalm. Rest, here, means standing still, and a learner keeps moving, from one strength to the next.
You can hear it at a siyum, the small celebration when someone finishes a tractate of Talmud. The words said at the end aren't goodbye.
They're hadran alakh: we will return to you. Finishing is a promise to come back.
So this new stretch, study for life, starts with no finish line.

teach.h: SIX DAYS OF LIVING WITH OTHERS.
teach.b: Before it, hold up the last six days. A rabbi and a Roman, two guards in an orchard: friends across faiths. Hillel's students saying the other view first: argue without hate.
A concern raised gently, in private: rebuke with love. Aaron walking back and forth: pursue peace.
Jeremiah's letter to the exiles: seek the city's peace. Rava's first question at the shop counter: keep doing justice. Six ways of living with other people, and none of them graduates you either.

how: Jewish learning has no graduation: study is meant to go on for life, and when someone finishes a tractate, a siyum is held where the finisher says hadran alakh, we will return to you.

games.q: your aunt finishes a whole tractate with her study group. at the party, a cousin asks: so you're done with it now? what do the words of the siyum answer?
o: not done: we will return to you.

done, until a rabbi tests her on it.

practice: Count on your fingers the people who taught you something that stuck: a parent, a coach, a friend, a grandparent, the writer of a book. Say each name quietly as you fold a finger down.
Then open one finger again, for whoever teaches you next.

wordCard.voice: A lifelong learner: someone who goes from strength to strength, finishing a text only to say, we will return to you.

orig.note: Aramaic: we will return to you; said on finishing a tractate.

carryVoice: Your line, and the week's: never graduated. Every finish is a promise to come back. That's the week.
